title: What the thread body needs
starter:
(* Names the body uses but does not define (other than loop_var), sorted, no repeats.
   body: (name, uses) statements, in order. *)
let free_vars (body : (string * string list) list) (loop_var : string) : string list =
  List.sort_uniq compare (List.concat_map snd body)
hints: Collect the defined names first: `List.map fst body`.
A use is free when it isn't defined in the body and isn't `loop_var`: `List.filter`.

answer.code:
(* Names the body uses but does not define (other than loop_var), sorted, no repeats.
   body: (name, uses) statements, in order. *)
let free_vars (body : (string * string list) list) (loop_var : string) : string list =
  let defined = List.map fst body in
  List.concat_map snd body
  |> List.filter (fun u -> not (List.mem u defined) && u <> loop_var)
  |> List.sort_uniq compare
answer.explain: This is closure conversion, the step every compiler takes when it turns a nested block into a separate function. In the rendered C, `b0` (a buffer), `v0` (a value computed before the loop) and enclosing ranges like `r3` are free in the body, so they go into the struct. Names the body defines, like private allocs and its own values, are declared inside the function instead.
